mainTopic: The מחלוקת over אימורים that left the עזרה, and the rules for which offering is brought first
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about אימורים that left the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled. The גמרא first suggests they argue about whether leaving the עזרה disqualifies the parts. רב פפא says instead that they argue about whether the זריקה works for parts that are still outside, and the גמרא shows this fits with his other statement about the שתי לחם. Next the גמרא goes back to the משנה's order of precedence: birds come before מנחות, and a מנחת חוטא comes before a מנחת נדבה. It then asks whether a מנחת סוטה or a מנחת נדבה comes first, and neither of the proofs it brings settles the question. The גמרא then finds the source for the rule that every חטאת comes before its עולה, even a bird חטאת before an animal עולה. A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר seems to put the יולדת's עולה first, but רבא explains that this is only the order of the words in the פסוק. The amud ends with a ברייתא that orders bulls, rams, sheep, and goats, which sets up a new challenge to that rule.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר versus רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. For אימורים that left the עזרה before the זריקה, one side (רבי אליעזר) says there is no liability for פיגול, נותר, or טמא. רבי עקיבא says there is מעילה, and there is liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one is not liable for them because of פיגול, נותר, or eating while impure. רבי עקיבא says: one does commit מעילה with them, and one is liable for them because of פיגול, נותר, and impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about sacrificial parts (אימורים) that were taken out of the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled. The first opinion says these parts carry none of the usual prohibitions, and רבי עקיבא says they carry all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of מעילה, פיגול, נותר, and טמא only apply to parts that the זריקה made into a valid part of the sacrifice. The first opinion holds these parts never became valid, so none of these rules apply. רבי עקיבא holds that they did, so every one of these rules applies. The next steps argue about why they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A sacrifice ruined by an improper intention about when it would be eaten; eating it brings כרת
Sacrificial meat left over past its time limit
Eating sacrificial meat while ritually impure
One commits מעילה, the misuse of הקדש property
One is liable to punishment

phrases.english: and one is not liable for them
phrases.notes: This is the end of the first opinion in the ברייתא, which is רבי אליעזר's. It is talking about אימורים that left the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled.

phrases.english: because of piggul, notar, or impurity;
Rabbi Akiva says:
one is liable for misuse of them,
and one is liable for them
because of piggul, notar, and impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא whose beginning appears before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אימורים that left before the זריקה, רבי אליעזר says there is no liability, and רבי עקיבא says there is מעילה and liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא.

steps.title: A suggestion: they argue whether leaving the עזרה disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the case is one where the אימורים were brought back into the עזרה before the זריקה. On that reading, the argument is whether leaving the עזרה disqualifies them permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not that they argue in a case where he then brought them back in? And this is what they argue about: one Sage holds that they are disqualified by having gone out, and the other Sage holds that they are not disqualified by having gone out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a way to read the ברייתא. It suggests the parts were returned to the עזרה, so the only question left is whether their trip outside ruined them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the parts were back inside during the זריקה, the only reason they could fail to count is that going out (יוצא) disqualified them. On this reading, רבי אליעזר holds that יוצא disqualifies, and רבי עקיבא holds that it does not. This would make the ברייתא a proof about the law of יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, is it not...?' The גמרא uses this to propose a reading, often as an attempted proof
He then brought them back in
They become disqualified
Something holy that has left its permitted area
'One Sage holds'

phrases.english: What, is it not
that they argue where he then brought them back in?
And this is what they argue about:
that one Sage holds they are disqualified by going out,
and the other Sage holds they are not disqualified by going out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from Step 1 as an argument about whether יוצא disqualifies.
steps.raayaObject: Whether אימורים become disqualified by leaving the עזרה (יוצא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, read as a case where the parts were brought back in

steps.title: רב פפא: they argue about parts still outside during the זריקה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the suggestion. When the parts were brought back in, everyone agrees. The argument is about parts still outside during the זריקה: does the זריקה work for something outside?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: where he then brought them back in, everyone agrees. Here they argue where the parts are still outside, and this is what they argue about: one Sage holds that the זריקה does not work for what has gone out, and the other Sage holds that the זריקה does work for what has gone out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the suggestion. He moves the argument to a different case, one where the parts are still outside the עזרה at the moment the blood is sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is no longer whether going out disqualifies. The question is whether the זריקה can reach parts that are not in the עזרה at that moment. רבי אליעזר says it cannot, and רבי עקיבא says it can. As a result, the ברייתא no longer proves anything about the law of יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Outside
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, which makes the sacrifice take effect
Is effective, works

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוֹעֶלֶת means 'is effective.' It has nothing to do with מעילה (misusing הקדש), even though the two words look alike.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
where he then brought them back in,
everyone agrees;
phrases.notes: He means everyone agrees the parts are fit.

phrases.english: and here they argue where the parts are outside,
and this is what they argue about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר אֵין זְרִיקָה מוֹעֶלֶת לַיּוֹצֵא,
phrases.english: that one Sage holds the sprinkling does not work for what went out,
and the other Sage holds the sprinkling does work for what went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּדַהֲדַר עַיְּילִינְהוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 2's reading by placing the case and the point of argument somewhere else.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא is about whether יוצא disqualifies parts that were brought back in.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case where the parts stayed outside, so the argument is about whether the זריקה works for them, not about יוצא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole question from 'Does leaving the עזרה ruin the parts?' to 'Can the זריקה reach parts that are outside?'

steps.title: רב פפא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב פפא himself said the opposite elsewhere. There he said that when the item is outside, everyone agrees, and the argument is only when it was brought back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it רב פפא himself who said: where they are outside, everyone agrees; they argue where he brought them back inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא with another statement of his own, which seems to reverse what he just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3, רב פפא said that everyone agrees when the item was brought back in, and the argument is about an item outside. In his other statement, about the שתי הלחם of שבועות, he said that everyone agrees when the item is outside, and the argument is about an item brought back in. These two statements cannot both be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely...' This opens a challenge from a known statement
Inside
The two loaves brought on שבועות together with two sheep

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rav Pappa who said:
phrases.notes: He is pointing to a different statement of רב פפא, about the שתי הלחם of שבועות.

phrases.english: where they are outside,
everyone agrees,
phrases.notes: Here everyone agrees the sprinkling does not make them fit, even רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: they argue where he brought them inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's explanation in Step 3 by contrasting it with his own statement elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that everyone agrees when the parts were brought back in, and the argument is about parts outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Self-contradiction. In the case of the שתי הלחם, רב פפא said the reverse: everyone agrees when the item is outside, and the argument is about an item brought back in.

steps.title: Two loaves versus the offering's own parts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's other statement was only about the שתי לחם, which are not part of the offering itself. For the אימורים, which are part of the offering, the argument is about when they are outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement was only about the two loaves, since they are not the offering itself. But the sacrificial parts are the offering itself, so the argument is about when they are outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 4. It shows that רב פפא's two statements are about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי לחם are only connected to the offering, so it is a real question whether the זריקה works for them when they were outside and then brought back in. The אימורים are the offering's own body, so once they are back inside, everyone agrees. The only argument is when they are still outside during the זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות together with the sheep offerings
The body of the offering itself
The parts of the offering that are burned on the altar
Outside (the עזרה)

steps.whatToRemember: For things that are part of the offering itself (the אימורים), everyone agrees they are fit once they are brought back in, and the argument is only when they are still outside. For things that are only connected to it (like the שתי לחם), everyone agrees the זריקה does not help when they are outside, and the argument is only when they were brought back in.

phrases.english: That statement applies only to the two loaves –
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's other statement, the one quoted in Step 4.

phrases.english: since they are not the offering itself;
but the sacrificial parts, which are the offering itself –
they disagree about a case where they are outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different subject matter (שתי לחם versus אימורים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's two statements contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Each statement is about a different kind of item, so there is no contradiction

steps.title: Shouldn't meal offerings come before birds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that birds come before מנחות. It challenges that מנחות should come first, since they are brought by both the ציבור and the יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says birds come first. On the contrary, meal offerings should come first, since they exist both for the community and for an individual!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about which offering is brought first and challenges one of its rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחות are brought both as communal offerings and as private ones, while bird offerings are only private. That seems to make מנחות more important, so they should come first.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird offerings
Meal (flour) offerings
On the contrary
The community / a private individual

phrases.english: Bird offerings precede, etc.
On the contrary – meal offerings should precede,
since they exist for the community as for an individual!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's order of precedence
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that birds come before מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחות have a feature that birds lack (they are also communal), so they should be more important

steps.title: Blood offerings are more important
steps.stepSummary: Even so, birds come first because they are a kind of blood offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, types of blood offerings are more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the משנה's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being brought by the ציבור is an advantage, but having blood that brings atonement is a bigger one. Birds have blood and מנחות do not, so birds come first.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Kinds of offerings that have blood
Are more important

phrases.english: Even so, types of blood offerings are more important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing advantages: one feature outweighs the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being communal should make מנחות come first
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood outweighs being communal, so birds come first

steps.title: Shouldn't the voluntary meal offering come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the sinner's מנחה comes before a voluntary מנחה. It challenges that the voluntary one should come first because it needs oil and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the sinner's meal offering comes first. On the contrary, the voluntary meal offering should come first, since it needs oil and frankincense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה and challenges it the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחת נדבה has more parts (oil and frankincense), while a מנחת חוטא is plain flour. That seems to make the voluntary one more complete and more important.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering brought by a poor sinner, made of plain flour
A voluntary meal offering
Oil and frankincense

phrases.english: The meal offering of a sinner, etc.
On the contrary – the voluntary meal offering should precede,
since it requires oil and frankincense!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as Step 6, now on the next rule of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מנחת חוטא comes before מנחת נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The voluntary מנחה has extra parts, so it should be more important

steps.title: Atonement comes first
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the sinner's מנחה comes first because it brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the sinner's meal offering, which comes because of a sin, is more important, because it atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the משנה's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil and frankincense are an advantage, but bringing כפרה is a bigger one. So the מנחת חוטא comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin
Brings atonement

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases the גמרא uses the same pattern: 'אדרבה' raises a competing advantage, and 'אפילו הכי' explains why the משנה's feature is stronger (blood, then atonement).

phrases.english: Even so, the meal offering of a sinner,
which comes because of a sin, is more important, because it atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא הַבָּאָה עַל חֵטְא עֲדִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing advantages: one feature outweighs the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil and frankincense should make the voluntary מנחה come first

steps.title: The סוטה's meal offering or a voluntary one: which comes first?
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא: which comes first, a מנחת סוטה or a מנחת נדבה? The voluntary one has oil and frankincense. The סוטה's offering comes to clarify a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a סוטה's meal offering and a voluntary meal offering, which comes first? Does the voluntary one come first because it needs oil and frankincense? Or does the סוטה's come first because it comes to clarify a sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question that the משנה does not answer. It lays out the reasons for both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת סוטה is plain, with no oil or frankincense, so it is like the sinner's offering in that way. But it does not atone; it only helps clarify whether there was a sin. So the גמרא asks whether clarifying a sin is strong enough to beat oil and frankincense.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
The meal offering of a woman suspected of adultery
Perhaps
To clarify (bring to light) a sin

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the מנחת סוטה is the same as the מנחת חוטא from Step 9. The sinner's offering atones, but the סוטה's offering only clarifies, which is why this is a new question.

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת סוֹטָה וּמִנְחַת נְדָבָה, אֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן קוֹדֶמֶת?
phrases.english: A sotah's meal offering and a voluntary meal offering, which of them comes first?
Does the voluntary meal offering come first –
since it requires oil and frankincense,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; read it simply as 'oil and frankincense.'

phrases.english: or perhaps the sotah's meal offering comes first –
since it comes to clarify a sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִנְחַת סוֹטָה וּמִנְחַת נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Steps 8-9 and asks about a case in between them
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether clarifying a sin gives precedence over having oil and frankincense

steps.title: Trying to prove from the משנה that a סוטה's offering does not come first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that a מנחת חוטא comes before a מנחת נדבה. It reads this as saying only the sinner's מנחה beats the voluntary one, but a מנחת סוטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the sinner's מנחה comes before the voluntary מנחה. So only the sinner's מנחה beats the voluntary one, but the סוטה's מנחה does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the איבעיא from Step 10 by making a careful reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the sinner's מנחה comes first because it brings atonement. A סוטה's מנחה does not atone, so the גמרא infers it would not come before a מנחת נדבה. On that reading, the voluntary מנחה, with its oil and frankincense, would win.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering a poor sinner brings in place of an animal
The barley meal offering of a woman suspected of adultery
But this one does not: a way of drawing an inference from what the text leaves out

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The meal offering of a sinner comes before a voluntary meal offering.

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא הוּא דְּקָדְמָה לְמִנְחַת נְדָבָה,
phrases.english: It is the sinner's meal offering that comes before the voluntary meal offering,
but the meal offering of a סוטה does not!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִנְחַת נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First attempt to settle the איבעיא from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנחת נדבה comes before a מנחת סוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ranking מנחת חוטא over מנחת נדבה, read as limited to offerings that atone.

steps.title: The משנה's reason is 'it comes because of a sin,' which fits the סוטה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה's reason is not 'it atones' but 'it comes because of a sin,' and a סוטה's מנחה also comes because of a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the משנה say 'because it atones'? It says 'because it comes because of a sin.' This one also comes because of a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 11 by looking closely at the exact reason the משנה gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in Step 11 only works if the reason is atonement. The משנה's actual wording points to the offering coming because of a sin. A סוטה's offering is also tied to a sin, so the משנה may include her too, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach...? A rhetorical question meaning 'that is not what it says'
Brings atonement
Comes because of a sin

steps.confusionAlert: Step 9 said the sinner's מנחה comes first 'because it atones,' but here the גמרא points out that the משנה's own wording is 'because it comes because of a sin.' This wording also fits the סוטה, even though her offering does not atone.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'because it brings atonement'?!
It teaches 'because it comes because of a sin,'
and this one also comes because of a sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the משנה's reason was atonement, when the stated reason is 'comes because of a sin,' which includes the סוטה.

steps.title: A second proof from a ברייתא: wheat comes before barley
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying one מנחה comes before another because it is made of wheat and the other of barley. It suggests this means the voluntary מנחה beats the סוטה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: this one comes before that one, since this one is from wheat and that one is from barley. Isn't it talking about a voluntary מנחה compared to a סוטה's מנחה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source to answer the איבעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה's מנחה is made of barley, while the other מנחות in this discussion are made of wheat. If the wheat מנחה in the ברייתא is the voluntary one, then the voluntary מנחה comes first, and the איבעיא is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat, which most מנחות are made from
Barley, which is used for the סוטה's מנחה
What, isn't it...? Proposing how to read a source

phrases.english: Come and hear:
This one comes before that one,
since this one comes from wheat
and that one comes from barley.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי, לָאו מִנְחַת נְדָבָה לְמִנְחַת סוֹטָה?
phrases.english: What, is it not talking about a voluntary meal offering compared to a סוטה's meal offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנחת נדבה comes before a מנחת סוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ranking a wheat מנחה over a barley one.

steps.title: Perhaps the ברייתא means the sinner's מנחה versus the סוטה's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The wheat מנחה in the ברייתא might be the sinner's, not the voluntary one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the sinner's מנחה compared to the סוטה's מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the ברייתא as talking about different offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sinner's מנחה is also made of wheat. If that is the offering the ברייתא means, it tells us nothing about the voluntary מנחה, so the איבעיא is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the גמרא is rejecting the proposed reading

phrases.english: No, it is talking about a sinner's meal offering compared to a סוטה's meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be talking about the מנחת חוטא, not the מנחת נדבה.

steps.title: But then the ברייתא should have said 'because it atones'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the ברייתא compares the sinner's מנחה to the סוטה's, it could have given a better reason: one atones and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: I could get that from the fact that this one atones and that one does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from Step 14, saying the ברייתא's reason doesn't fit it well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא meant the sinner's מנחה, its strongest reason would be atonement. Since it used 'wheat versus barley' instead, it seems it must mean a pair where atonement isn't a factor, like the voluntary מנחה and the סוטה's.

keyTerms.meaning: I could get it from [another reason]: why give this reason when a stronger one is available?
It atones (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: I could get it from the fact
that this one atones
and that one does not atone!

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיפּוֹק לִי דְּהָא מְכַפְּרָא וְהָא לָא מְכַפְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as מנחת חוטא versus מנחת סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source would give the most obvious reason. Atonement is more obvious here than wheat versus barley, so the ברייתא must not mean the מנחת חוטא.

steps.title: The same problem hits the voluntary-מנחה reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the challenge around. If the ברייתא meant the voluntary מנחה, it also had a better reason available: oil and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what, it means a voluntary מנחה? I could get that from the fact that this one needs oil and frankincense and that one does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the challenge from Step 15 works just as well against the other reading. This sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The voluntary מנחה has oil and frankincense, and the סוטה's has neither. That would also be a clear reason. So both readings have the same 'why not the other reason?' problem, which means that problem cannot decide between them.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather what? Turning the same challenge against the other side
Oil and frankincense, which are added to most מנחות
Requires

phrases.english: But rather what, it means a voluntary meal offering?

phrases.aramaic: תִּיפּוֹק לִי דְּזוֹ טְעוּנָה שֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה,
phrases.english: I could get that from the fact that this one requires oil and frankincense,
and that one does not require oil and frankincense!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by showing its challenge works just as well against the other reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as מנחת נדבה versus מנחת סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading also skips an obvious reason (oil and frankincense), so the 'better reason' argument proves nothing.

steps.title: The ברייתא just named one of two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that whichever pair the ברייתא means, it simply chose one of two good reasons. So the missing reason proves nothing, and the ברייתא does not settle the איבעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it took one of two reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up: leaving out a second reason is normal, so we can't tell which pair the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both readings leave out a second reason, leaving one out is not unusual. The ברייתא can still be read as the sinner's מנחה versus the סוטה's, so the proof from Step 13 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: One of two reasons
It took, meaning it cited

steps.whatToRemember: Neither the משנה nor the ברייתא settles whether a מנחת סוטה or a מנחת נדבה comes first. A source that gives only one reason when it could have given two proves nothing, because sources often mention just one.

phrases.english: Rather, it cited one of two reasons.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; it means 'took' or 'cited'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the back-and-forth in Steps 15 and 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא simply named one of two reasons, so it cannot prove that a מנחת נדבה comes before a מנחת סוטה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the bird sin offering comes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a bird חטאת comes first and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A bird sin offering comes first, etc.' Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a bird חטאת is offered before a burnt offering, even before an animal עולה. 'מנא הני מילי' asks for the Torah source behind that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering brought from a bird
Comes first, takes priority
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: 'The bird sin offering comes first, etc.'
From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the מנחה discussion ended in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the rule that a bird חטאת comes before an עולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא points out that a phrase in the פסוק seems extra
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes 'he shall offer the חטאת first' and asks why it is needed, since another פסוק already says the second bird is the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall offer the one for the sin offering first.' Why does the Torah need to say this? It is not needed to teach that the חטאת is offered first, because the Torah already said: 'And the second he shall make a burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא points out that the word 'first' seems unneeded, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About the poor sinner's two birds, ויקרא 5:10 already calls the עולה 'the second' bird. That already tells us the חטאת comes first. So the word 'first' in 5:8 looks extra and must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
First
And the second he shall make a burnt offering

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'And he shall offer the one for the sin offering first'
Why does the verse need to say this?
For the verse does not need to say it
to teach that it is offered first,
since it was already said:
'And the second he shall make a burnt offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 18 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the word 'first' in ויקרא 5:8, which is extra and so teaches a wider rule.

steps.title: The extra word sets up a general rule for every חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The extra word makes a בנה אב: every חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it, even a bird חטאת before an animal עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this phrase sets up a general rule for all sin offerings: they come before the burnt offerings brought with them. This holds for a bird sin offering with a bird burnt offering, for an animal sin offering with an animal burnt offering, and even for a bird sin offering with an animal burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what the extra word teaches. It is a general rule that applies to every חטאת, not only to the poor sinner's two birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the order of the poor sinner's birds was already known, 'first' is used as a pattern for all cases. The new part is the mixed case: even a lowly bird חטאת comes before a more valuable animal עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a general rule (a model case that teaches other cases)
A burnt offering brought from an animal
That are brought together with them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that a bird חטאת comes before even an animal עולה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא זֶה בָּנָה אָב לְכׇל חַטָּאוֹת
phrases.english: Rather, this set up a general rule for all sin offerings
that they come before the burnt offerings that are brought with them
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'burnt offering' (round brackets); the corrected wording is the plural 'burnt offerings' (square brackets).

phrases.english: whether a bird sin offering with a bird burnt offering,
or an animal sin offering with an animal burnt offering,
and even a bird sin offering with an animal burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא זֶה בָּנָה אָב לְכׇל חַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own question about why the word 'first' is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word is read as a general rule for all cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'first' seemed unneeded, since 'the second' already showed the order.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that every חטאת comes before its עולה, including a bird חטאת before an animal עולה.

steps.title: Summary: which source teaches which case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sorts out the three cases: bird and bird from 'the second', animal and animal from the לויים, bird and animal from the בנה אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: So: a bird sin offering before a bird burnt offering is learned from 'and the second'. An animal sin offering before an animal burnt offering is learned from the fact that the Merciful One extended the rule. A bird sin offering before an animal burnt offering is learned from 'this set up a general rule'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives each of the three cases its own source. It shows that the בנה אב is truly needed only for the mixed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the three cases already had sources, one from ויקרא 5:10 and one from the earlier discussion of the לויים. That leaves the mixed case of a bird חטאת and an animal עולה as the real new teaching of the בנה אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, so
The Merciful One (the Torah, ה׳)
Here: extended, included more cases (not the title 'רבי')

steps.whatToRemember: Bird before bird: 'the second'. Animal before animal: the rule extended from the לויים. Bird חטאת before animal עולה: the בנה אב from the extra word 'first'.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מִדְּרַבִּי does not mean 'from a רבי'. It comes from a word meaning 'to include' or 'to extend': the Torah extended the rule.

phrases.english: Therefore, a bird sin offering with a bird burnt offering
is learned from 'and the second',
an animal sin offering with an animal burnt offering
is learned from the fact that the Merciful One extended the rule,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier learning from the לויים' offerings, where the Torah widened the rule to other cases.

phrases.english: a bird sin offering with an animal burnt offering
is learned from 'this set up a general rule'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the ברייתא by assigning a source to each case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each case of a חטאת before an עולה has its own source. The בנה אב is needed for the bird חטאת before an animal עולה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: in the case of the יולדת, the burnt offering comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's teaching: wherever a bird חטאת takes the place of an animal one, the חטאת comes first, but in the case of the יולדת the עולה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says: Anywhere the sin offering was switched, the sin offering comes first. But here, with a woman who gave birth, the burnt offering comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with 'תא שמע' and brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the rule from step 20 that every חטאת comes first. The ברייתא continues in the next step, and רבא answers the clash in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a poor person brings birds instead of an animal, the חטאת is offered first. רבי אליעזר says the יולדת is different: her עולה comes first. So the general rule about the order has at least one case that works differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Was switched or exchanged (a bird brought in place of an animal)
A woman who has given birth

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says:
Every place where the sin offering was switched,
phrases.notes: He means a case where a poor person brings a bird in place of an animal.

phrases.english: the sin offering comes first,
but here (with a woman who gave birth) the burnt offering comes first.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, 'here' means the case of the יולדת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the general rule that a חטאת comes first, a new source shows a case where the עולה comes first.
steps.raayaObject: The order of the חטאת and the עולה when birds are brought in place of animals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי אליעזר's view on the יולדת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנה אב (step 20) that every חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר says that for the יולדת the עולה comes first. That seems to break the rule that every חטאת comes first.

steps.title: Two more reasons the יולדת's עולה seems to come first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's ברייתא continues: a חטאת for a sin comes first, and two birds replacing an animal חטאת put the חטאת first. The יולדת is different on both counts, so her עולה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everywhere a חטאת comes because of a sin, the חטאת comes first, but here the עולה comes first. And everywhere two birds come in place of an animal חטאת, the חטאת comes first, but here the עולה comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting רבי אליעזר's ברייתא from the last step. It adds two more ways the יולדת is different from other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: the יולדת's חטאת is not brought for a sin; it comes to make her pure. Reason two: her bird חטאת is not a cheaper swap for an animal, because even a rich יולדת brings a bird חטאת. Read plainly, this seems to clash with the בנה אב from step 20, which says every חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin
But here (in the case of the יולדת)
In place of
A woman who gave birth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the יולדת's חטאת is not really a חטאת. It is fully a חטאת. The ברייתא only says it is unusual because it is not brought for a sin and does not replace an animal.

phrases.english: Every place where it comes because of a sin –
the חטאת comes first,
but here the עולה comes first;
phrases.notes: "Here" means the יולדת. Her חטאת makes her pure; it is not brought for a sin.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁנַיִם בָּאִים תַּחַת חַטָּאת –
phrases.english: and every place where two come in place of a חטאת –
phrases.notes: "Two" means two birds that a poor person brings in place of an animal חטאת.

phrases.english: the חטאת comes first,
but here the עולה comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי אליעזר quoted in step 22, adding two more reasons.
steps.raayaObject: That in the case of the יולדת the עולה is offered before the חטאת
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנה אב (step 20) that every חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives two more reasons why the יולדת's עולה comes first. Read plainly, this is a real exception to the rule that every חטאת comes first.

steps.title: רבא: the עולה comes first only in the wording of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the פסוק mentions the יולדת's עולה first only in how it is written. In practice her חטאת is still offered first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the פסוק put the עולה first only for the reading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the clash between רבי אליעזר's ברייתא and the rule that a חטאת always comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's "the עולה comes first" means only that the פסוק names the עולה first. It does not mean the עולה is offered first. So the בנה אב stays in place: even for the יולדת, the חטאת is offered first.

keyTerms.meaning: For its reading, in the wording of the פסוק
Put it first
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: For the יולדת, the עולה is written first but the חטאת is offered first. The rule that a חטאת comes before its עולה holds everywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the בנה אב from step 20 as a rule with no exceptions in practice, even for the יולדת.

phrases.english: רבא said:
The פסוק put it first only for its reading.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:6 mentions the יולדת's עולה before her חטאת, but that is just the order of the words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash raised by the ברייתא in steps 22-23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: "comes first" refers to the order in the פסוק, not the order of offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יולדת actually offers her עולה before her חטאת, which breaks the בנה אב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה is only written first; in practice her חטאת is offered first, like every other חטאת.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about the order of bulls, rams, sheep and goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets the order of different animal offerings: bulls, then rams, then sheep, then goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: bulls come before rams, rams come before sheep, and sheep come before goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with "come and hear" and quotes a new ברייתא. It is setting up its next move, a question about this order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא orders offerings by type of animal, from the largest to the smallest. The goats come last, even though the goats in these lists are usually brought as a חטאת while the bulls, rams, and sheep are עולות. That seems to clash with the rule that a חטאת comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls
Rams
Sheep (lambs)
Male goats

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Bulls come before rams,
and rams come before sheep,
sheep before goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clash over the יולדת is settled, the גמרא brings a new source to test the rule that a חטאת comes first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule (step 20) that a חטאת comes before the עולה brought with it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא orders offerings by type of animal and puts goats last. The גמרא is setting up a question about whether this fits the rule that a חטאת comes first.
